title: Fellowship Steps
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Lydia, still angry at Barnabas after a church fellowship chili cook-off dispute, promised to pay Paul $10,000 if he would kill Barnabas in any manner that could not be traced to her. Paul bought a gun and watched Barnabas’s house for an opportunity to shoot him.

One evening, unaware of Paul’s presence, Barnabas tripped as he was walking toward his house, fell, and hit his head against the front steps. Believing that Barnabas was unconscious, Paul ran over to him and shot him twice in the chest. When Lydia learned of Barnabas’s death, she paid Paul $10,000. A medical examiner determined that Barnabas was already dead when Paul shot him.

The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness. What is the most serious crime of which Lydia properly could be convicted?
call: The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness. What is the most serious crime of which Lydia properly could be convicted?
rightExplanation:
B is correct. Lydia’s hired killer acted with the purpose to kill and took a direct, substantial step by watching Barnabas’s house, running to him, and shooting him in the chest. Murder fails because Barnabas was already dead when Paul shot him, so Paul’s shots did not cause Barnabas’s death. But the failed killing still supports attempted murder.

Gold Key: A completed murder needs a death caused by the defendant’s conduct; attempted murder can still exist when the actor believed the victim was alive and acted to kill.
Silver Key: The answer choices are a descending crime ladder. Once the top completed-crime rung falls and the attempt rung survives, do not drop to the lower true-but-less-serious inchoate crimes.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text:
A is not safe because it needs the completed-result fact. The stem gives the opposite: Barnabas was already dead when shot.
C and D are lower ladder rungs. They remain plausible only if B fails.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text:
A and B fight on one axis: completed death caused by the shooter vs. attempted killing despite failed result.
Splitting fact: medical examiner says Barnabas was already dead when Paul shot him.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Apply the descending-ladder call. Once A falls and B survives, C and D are true-but-not-most-serious.

studentScript: Death happened, but Paul did not cause it. Murder falls. Paul believed Barnabas was alive and shot to kill. Attempt survives. The ladder says stop at the highest valid crime: B.

A.signal: The medical-examiner fact breaks completed causation.
A.lawyer: No murder because the death was not caused by Paul’s shots; Barnabas was already dead.

B.signal: A falls on causation; B survives on intent plus substantial step.
B.lawyer: Attempted murder is proper because Paul believed Barnabas was alive and acted to kill; Lydia intentionally procured and paid for that killing attempt.

C.signal: The call asks most serious; conspiracy is below attempted murder in the listed ladder.
C.lawyer: The facts may support conspiracy, but it is not the most serious proper conviction listed.

D.signal: Lydia did solicit, but the ladder has higher valid crimes.
D.lawyer: Solicitation is lower than conspiracy and attempted murder; it is not the most serious proper conviction.

goldKeys.statement: No completed murder unless the defendant’s conduct causes the victim’s death; but shooting a person believed alive can still be attempted murder even if the victim was already dead.
goldKeys.trigger: Medical examiner says the target was already dead when shot.
goldKeys.unlocks: A/B trap: murder vs attempted murder
goldKeys.authority: People v. Dlugash; Model Penal Code § 5.01

goldKeys.statement: A person who intentionally hires or aids another to commit a killing can be liable for the attempt when the killing fails after a substantial step.
goldKeys.trigger: Instigator pays another to kill, and the hired actor acts toward the killing.
goldKeys.unlocks: Why Lydia reaches attempted murder rather than only solicitation or conspiracy.

silverKeys.statement: When the call says the crimes are listed in descending order, stop at the first legally valid rung; lower true crimes become not responsive.
silverKeys.trigger: Call expressly says descending order of seriousness.

remediation.title: Dead target, live attempt
remediation.signal: Victim already dead before the killer’s act.
remediation.studentMove: Separate completed-result crime from attempt, then use the descending ladder.
remediation.tinyRule: No causation means no murder; belief plus substantial step means attempt.
remediation.trap: Picking murder because someone died, or conspiracy because the plot was real.
